execution_context.file_location: Garmin South African shopping site (injected JavaScript on payment page)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form submission, collects payment and personal data from form fields, and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating sensitive payment and personal data to an external domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce scripts should only send payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form data may be sent to payment gateways or fraud detection services, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted or hardcoded external domains

execution_context.file_location: Email attachment (PDF file with embedded executable payload)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user opens the disguised PDF, the executable overwrites all user files with garbage data and displays a fake ransomware message.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting all user files with random data is destructive and not a legitimate operation for any user-facing application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A job application PDF should not execute code or modify user files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for this behavior in a PDF or job application context.
key_indicators: Display of ransom note after destruction

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the shopping site’s payment page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment and personal data from customers.

attack_chain.action: JavaScript code captures form data and sends it to an attacker-controlled server.
Victim receives a spam email with a PDF attachment that is actually an executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the attachment, triggering the payload.

attack_chain.action: Executable overwrites all user files with garbage and displays a fake ransom note.
attack_chain.leads_to: Permanent data loss and attempted extortion.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code capturing and exfiltrating form data on payment pages
Network requests from client-side scripts to untrusted or hardcoded domains
Executable files disguised as PDFs in email attachments
Mass file overwrite operations followed by ransom note display
file_indicators: Unexpected JavaScript changes on payment/checkout pages
Files with random or garbage content after opening suspicious attachments
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate business
Connections to known malicious exfiltration endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized JavaScript changes on sensitive web pages, especially those that access form fields and send data to unknown domains. Flag email attachments with double extensions or executable content masquerading as documents. Detect mass file overwrite operations and the appearance of ransom notes following suspicious file activity.
